sources.title: Stock Market Recap Nov 6, 2026: Tech Stocks Rebound, but Wall Street Ends Its Worst Week Since June
U.S. adds 165,000 jobs in October as December Fed hike odds climb
Fed rate hike odds jump after October jobs report
Lockheed Martin, RTX, Northrop Stocks Fall After Democratic Midterm Sweep
Democratic Midterm Sweep Rattles Defense Stocks; Wolfe Calls Selloff a Buying Opportunity

market_view: The market is stressed. The VIX fear gauge is at 25.6, credit spreads are widening, and the S&P 500 is only about 1% above its 200-day average after its worst week since June. Democrats swept the midterms, which hit AI-infrastructure stocks (new limits on data-center building) and defense stocks (Trump's $1.5T defense budget looks doomed). On Thursday the Nasdaq fell about 5.5% and chip stocks about 12%; Friday won back only part of that. October jobs came in hot (+165k against about 60k expected), pushing December rate-hike odds to about 77%. That means October CPI on Nov 10 can move the market sharply in either direction. The portfolio already leans defensive: healthcare, consumer staples, Walmart, Treasuries and modest defense stocks, with little tech or chip exposure. So this is a day to hold, not to chase rebounds or add risk before CPI.
key_drivers: 2026-11-06: October jobs +165k vs ~60k expected, unemployment 4.1%; CME FedWatch/Polymarket odds of a December hike rose to ~77%
2026-11-04/05: Democratic midterm sweep; Nasdaq -5.5% and chips -12% on Thursday on AI capex and data-center restriction worries

2026-11-04: defense stocks fell (LMT down as much as 7%, NOC ~4-5%) on doubts about the $1.5T defense budget; Wolfe Research calls it a buying opportunity, and multiyear programs (F-35, B-21) are insulated
Week of Nov 2-6: S&P 500 -2.7%, Nasdaq -3.4%; defensive sectors (staples, healthcare) still in uptrends
2026-11-06: Lilly-Hims & Hers direct-access deal for Zepbound/orforglipron supports LLY's volume story

positions.thesis: Healthcare has been the leading defensive sector (16.6% above its 200-day average) during a tech-led selloff. It is low-beta exposure that is not just more S&P 500.
positions.exit_plan: Sell if it closes below its 50-day average while the market recovers, or if Democratic drug-pricing proposals gain traction.
positions.plain_reason: Healthcare companies tend to hold up when the market is nervous.

positions.thesis: The strong jobs report and low layoffs support consumer spending into the holidays. Retail is in an uptrend and has little AI-capex exposure.
positions.exit_plan: Sell on a clear consumer slowdown in the data, or a close below the 200-day average.
positions.plain_reason: Shoppers still have jobs and are spending ahead of the holidays.

positions.thesis: A Treasury hedge against an equity drawdown. Yields have fallen during the risk-off move.
positions.exit_plan: Cut if a hot CPI on Nov 10 drives a sharp rise in yields while stocks hold up.
positions.plain_reason: Government bonds act as a cushion if stocks keep falling.

positions.thesis: Obesity-drug leader with momentum (23% above its 200-day average). The Hims & Hers deal widens self-pay access. It does not depend on AI capex.
positions.exit_plan: Sell on a negative orforglipron/regulatory surprise or a drug-pricing policy shock; otherwise let the trailing stop work.
positions.plain_reason: Its weight-loss drugs keep winning customers no matter what tech does.

positions.thesis: Defensive retailer gaining market share, in a strong trend. It reports Q3 on Nov 19 (expected); held as a quality defensive into the report.
positions.exit_plan: Reassess after the Nov 19 earnings; sell on weak guidance or a close below the 50-day average.
positions.plain_reason: Walmart sells everyday goods people buy even in rough times.

positions.thesis: Low-beta consumer staple in a steady uptrend, which diversifies away from tech beta.
positions.exit_plan: Sell if staples lose relative strength once the market turns risk-on.
positions.plain_reason: People keep buying soap and diapers in any economy.

positions.thesis: Turnaround story with momentum (15% above its 200-day average), less tied to the AI cycle.
positions.exit_plan: Sell on a close back below its 50-day average or a trailing-stop hit.
positions.plain_reason: The company's turnaround is working and the stock keeps climbing.

positions.thesis: Nuclear and B-21 programs are the least exposed to budget cuts from a Democratic Congress, and the post-election drop looks overdone. Held for weeks, not days.
positions.exit_plan: Sell if Congress moves to cut its core programs, or on a trailing-stop hit.
positions.plain_reason: Its long-term military contracts are hard for Congress to cancel.

positions.thesis: Record $292B backlog and multiyear F-35 work. The midterm selloff hit budget growth expectations more than current business. Kept small.
positions.exit_plan: Exit if it closes below the 200-day average, or if there are clear signs of program cuts in early-2027 appropriations.
positions.plain_reason: It has years of orders already booked despite political noise.

positions.thesis: Quality mega-cap that is holding its trend (14.7% above its 200-day average) while other tech breaks down. Record share of smartphone revenue.
positions.exit_plan: Sell on a close below its 50-day average along with weakening iPhone demand data.
positions.plain_reason: Apple's phones still earn about half of all smartphone revenue worldwide.

plain_summary: No trades today: we keep our safer holdings and wait for the inflation report on Tuesday.
